description: Port load_baseline/save_baseline/delta. Baseline is JSON at <git-dir>/claude-token-baseline.json (git-dir resolved absolutely). delta clamps each component at >= 0 so a transcript rotation can never produce a negative trailer. Handle the first-run case: no baseline -> save current cumulative, emit a zero delta with source '<source>:baseline-initialised'.

description:
User reports (2026-07-14): after replacing fhr_sim_v2's six-group SixGroupPRKE kinetics with teh-o-prke's Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper (op-dt3.7 / prke_backend/mod.rs), the reactor power oscillates a lot during operation. The old PRKE-based fhr_sim_v2 did not oscillate.

Likely root cause (physics, not a code bug): Nordheim-Fuchs is a PROMPT-only excursion model -- it neglects delayed-neutron precursor dynamics entirely (documented limitation in its module doc and the user-supplied design scaffold: 'Delayed-neutron-driven operational transients should remain in the PRKE subsystem'). The old six-group PRKE carried six delayed-neutron precursor groups whose decay constants act as a low-pass filter / inertia that damps the reactivity-power-temperature feedback loop. Nordheim-Fuchs has none of that damping, so the fuel-temperature feedback loop (alpha_f*(T-T_ref) -> power -> pebble-bed heating -> T) rings.

Contributing coupling detail in the fhr_sim_v2 wiring: each 1ms step, prke_backend overwrites nordheim_fuchs.fuel_temperature with the pebble-bed TH model's temperature (the authoritative, heat-removal-aware value), then steps NF. NF also advances T internally via its own adiabatic C_f dT/dt = P. The two temperature models can disagree step-to-step, feeding the oscillation.

Candidate fixes (not yet chosen -- discuss with user):
(a) Add the 'Delayed Neutron Layer' from the outram-park-dt-plan architecture (a precursor transfer-function bank, e.g. via chem-eng transfer functions) between the prompt-excursion layer and the TH layer, restoring delayed-neutron damping.
(b) Use Nordheim-Fuchs only for prompt-critical excursion DEMOS (its intended purpose) and keep six-group PRKE for quasi-steady operation in fhr_sim_v2 -- i.e. the NF swap may be the wrong model for this always-on operational sim.
(c) Relax/filter the pebble-bed->NF fuel-temperature hand-off and/or the reactivity feedback to damp the loop numerically (a band-aid, not physical).

Regression reference: git 86ccb04 (the NF swap) + 540fd45; the pre-swap PRKE version is the parent commit of 86ccb04's prke_backend.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-15 via option (a): added teh_o_prke::delayed_neutron_layer::DelayedNeutronLayer (5 first-order TransferFnFirstOrder lags) and wired it into fhr_sim_v2 prke_backend as a Lie-split point-kinetics update: NF advances the prompt part, the layer supplies the delayed source S=sum lambda_i C_i, total P = P_prompt + S*dt fed back to NF and to TH. Reconciled fuel-temp handoff: pebble bed is sole authoritative T owner; NF C_f aligned to pebble-bed heat capacity (8000kg*340). Headless regression (isolated kinetics+pebble-bed loop, dt=5ms, 80s, coolant fixed): prompt-only tail peak-to-peak = 194.2 MW on 31.8 MW mean (rings); with delayed layer = 0.0086 MW on 35.8 MW mean (22543x damping, settles). Regression tests added in both fhr_sim_v2 copies (engine canonical + tampines mirror): oscillation_regression::{delayed_neutron_layer_damps_power_oscillation, shipped_prke_timestep_settles}. Both fhr_sim_v2 copies build --release. beta_i/lambda_i from teh-o-prke six_group_constants U-235, reduced 6->5 groups (merged two fastest).

title: fhr_sim_v2 reactor power oscillates after Nordheim-Fuchs kinetics swap (no delayed-neutron damping)

description:
Replaces the mistaken op-jyyp.4, which proposed adding a gas arm to the TUAS Material enum. Maintainer ruling 2026-08-11: TUAS is for SALT solvers only and must never gain a gas arm; gas belongs in tampines.

THE NEED. An HTR-10 primary circuit is a helium loop at 3.0 MPa flowing 4.3 kg/s between 250 C and 700 C. Nothing in the workspace can currently model that with prebuilt components: TUAS has the component library but is salt-scoped, and tampines has the composition role but its component layer returns not-implemented for everything except Pipe::step.

WHAT TO BUILD. A gas-phase component layer in crates/tampines that can represent a forced-convection helium circuit: pipe/duct pressure drop and heat transfer for a compressible gas, the pebble-bed core as a porous component, and the circulator. Properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, which already carries a full Helmholtz EOS for helium plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and thermal-conductivity correlations tested against tabulated reference states — consume those, do not reimplement or hardcode.

KNOWN DEFECT TO FIX WHILE HERE. htgr_sim_v1 currently hardcodes a constant helium viscosity despite the real correlation existing one crate away in coolprop. That shortcut should not survive into the gas layer.

RELATED WORK ALREADY LANDED. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/ carries the cited HTR-10 design point and a verified KTA packed-bed pressure-drop implementation (reproduces the VTB gold values to every quoted digit). The gas layer should consume that rather than re-deriving it.

ALSO NOTE op-ql8 — tampines already has an open bead to wire the tested dwsim flash and finish the NotYetImplemented component wrappers. These two overlap; sequence them together rather than in conflict.

Do not widen TUAS. If a change appears to require touching tuas_boussinesq_solver Material enum, stop and reconsider the design.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
SCOPE REFINEMENT from the maintainer, 2026-08-11: TUAS is not salt-only — it also does LIQUID METAL, even though salt was the original intent. So the boundary that matters is PHASE, not chemistry: TUAS covers LIQUIDS (molten salts and liquid metals), and GAS is the excluded phase.

That makes the ruling sharper rather than weaker. Do not read the earlier note on op-jyyp.4 as 'TUAS is for salt' — read it as 'TUAS is for liquids, and helium is not a liquid'. Adding a liquid-metal coolant to TUAS would be in scope; adding a gas arm is not, and that is why the HTR-10 helium circuit belongs in tampines.

Practical consequence for whoever implements this bead: do not try to generalise the TUAS Material enum into a phase-generic abstraction as a way of sneaking gas in. The liquid assumption is baked into the solver itself — TUAS is the Thermo-hydraulic Uniphase Advection and Convection Solver built on the Boussinesq approximation, which assumes small density variation. Helium at 3.0 MPa over a 250-700 C range varies in density by roughly a factor of two across the core, so the Boussinesq assumption does not hold for it. The exclusion is physical, not merely organisational.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
FINAL SCOPE FRAMING from the maintainer, 2026-08-11 — supersedes the two notes above, which were successively too narrow:

TUAS handles anything SINGLE-PHASE and NEARLY INCOMPRESSIBLE. That is liquids in practice — molten salts and liquid metals. An incompressible gas would technically fit the solver, but that restriction is severe enough that the maintainer explicitly does NOT want gas promised as a TUAS capability. Treat gas as out of scope for TUAS, full stop.

TAMPINES IS THE SUPERSET THAT INCLUDES TUAS. That is the architectural point and it resolves the whole question: gas support does not require widening TUAS, because tampines already sits above it and composes it alongside outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Adding a gas layer at the tampines level is the natural place for it, not a workaround.

So the correct reading of this bead is not 'TUAS cannot do it, so find somewhere else'. It is 'tampines is where the superset lives, and a compressible helium circuit is a superset capability'.

Physical justification, unchanged: helium at 3.0 MPa across 250-700 C varies in density by roughly a factor of two through the core, so the nearly-incompressible assumption TUAS is built on genuinely does not hold for the HTR-10 primary circuit.

title: tampines: gas-phase component layer for the HTR-10 helium primary circuit

description: Issue #30 comment 2026-08-22 03:06 UTC floats a parallelogram (not just axis-aligned box) calibration for plots photographed/scanned off-axis. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/calibration.rs's PlotCalibration is strictly axis-aligned today (AxisCalibration per axis, pixel = column for x / row for y; see module doc + tests) -- there is no 2D projective or affine-from-4-points transform anywhere in the digitiser. Adding one is a DigitisedDataset schema change (DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in dataset.rs), since PlotCalibration is serialized to the on-disk JSON. Needs a maintainer call before implementation: is this in scope now, and if so does the new calibration variant coexist with the axis-aligned one (enum-dispatched, per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule) or replace it. Blocks nothing else in the op-9c2e tree; the axis-aligned persistent-box UX (sibling bead) ships independently.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
RECOMMENDATION, not a decision -- flagging this as a genuine blocker for the maintainer rather than deciding unilaterally, per the criteria that make it different from op-6ez3/op-9bvi (which I did decide): this one (a) changes a persisted on-disk schema (DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, PlotCalibration becomes an enum with a new variant) affecting every previously-exported dataset's re-readability, and (b) blocks nothing else in the op-9c2e tree today -- the axis-aligned persistent draggable box (op-zfnh, shipped) already solves the bulk of the practical complaint (no more one-click-per-corner), and per the bead's own description a parallelogram variant would coexist with, not replace, axis-aligned calibration.

My recommendation, for whenever the maintainer wants to pick this up: enum-dispatch per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule --

  pub enum PlotCalibration {
      AxisAligned(AxisCalibration, AxisCalibration),  // today's shape, renamed as a variant
      Parallelogram { corners: [PixelPoint; 4], data_corners: [(f64, f64); 4] },
  }

with point_at() matching on the variant (axis-aligned: today's per-axis linear/log interpolation, unchanged; parallelogram: a bilinear or full 2D projective (homography) map from the pixel quadrilateral to the data-space quadrilateral -- projective is the more correct choice if the plot was genuinely photographed at an angle with perspective foreshortening, bilinear is simpler and adequate for a merely-skewed-but-not-perspective scan). DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2, with read_json handling both old (implicit AxisAligned) and new records for backward read compatibility -- write path always emits the new shape.

Not implemented. Left open pending maintainer input on: (1) is this worth the schema churn given op-zfnh already shipped, (2) bilinear vs full projective, (3) whether AxisAligned stays the default/only option for existing UX and Parallelogram is opt-in via a toggle, or whether the draggable box should just always be a freely-skewable quadrilateral (simpler UI, but changes existing muscle memory for the common axis-aligned case).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented. Per explicit maintainer instruction: "parallelogram mode and rectangle mode should be selectable enums. so that we don't break old code" -- exactly the enum-dispatched shape recommended in the earlier comment, now built.

crates/kovan/src/digitiser/calibration.rs:
- `PlotCalibration` is now an enum: `AxisAligned { x, y }` (the original shape, unchanged behaviour) and `Parallelogram(ParallelogramCalibration)` (new).
- **Backward compatibility via `#[serde(untagged)]`**: `AxisAligned` serialises to byte-identical `{"x": ..., "y": ...}` JSON -- every dataset already on disk under `DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 still deserialises unchanged, no migration, no version bump needed (verified: `read_json`'s schema_version check is a top-level dataset field untouched by this change). Test: `old_flat_json_still_deserialises_as_axis_aligned`.
- `ParallelogramCalibration`: 4 pixel-space corners mapped to the unit square via a 2D projective transform (homography, solved via an 8x8 Gauss-Jordan linear system -- the standard "photographed rectangle" perspective-correction map), then the *same* per-axis linear/log interpolation `AxisCalibration` already implements and tests. Validated constructor (`new`) rejects degenerate corners, non-finite/coincident values, and non-positive log-axis references, mirroring `AxisCalibration::new`'s own rules. 12 new calibration tests: round-trip, corner-to-reference-value mapping, log-axis correctness, degenerate-input rejection, and a sanity check that a parallelogram over an actual rectangle reproduces `AxisAligned`'s numbers exactly.
- `xy_uncertainty_interval` (dataset.rs) generalises the existing per-axis `uncertainty_interval` to the enum: `AxisAligned` delegates unchanged (byte-identical behaviour); `Parallelogram` perturbs column/row and reads the value spread off `point_at` (documented simplification, same "treat x/y as independent" spirit the original already has).

GUI (crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/mod.rs): a real, working "selectable" surface, not just internal plumbing --
- New "Calibration shape" toggle (Rectangle | Parallelogram) in the side panel.
- Rectangle mode: completely unchanged (same 4 lines, same corner-drag from the earlier round).
- Parallelogram mode: 4 freely-draggable corners (no rectilinear constraint), drawn as a skewed quad outline with the same corner-handle styling: drag any corner independently to skew the box to match an off-angle photo.
- Same 4 data-value text fields reused in both modes (X1/X2/Y1/Y2 -- left/right/bottom/top).
- Auto-trace correctly rejects Parallelogram mode with a clear message (the automatic column/row scan is inherently axis-aligned -- same boundary as the CLI/TUI automatic pipeline in `auto.rs`, now documented there too) and points the operator at hand-placing points instead.

Downstream call sites fixed to keep AxisAligned behaviour byte-identical: `auto.rs` (CLI/TUI automatic pipeline, stays AxisAligned-only by design), `synthetic.rs` (test-fixture generator, AxisAligned-only), `tui/digitiser.rs` (hand-placed point nudging, now calibration-shape-agnostic via the new PlotCalibration-level `pixel_at`/`xy_uncertainty_interval` methods), `dataset.rs` (CSV provenance header now branches on variant to describe either shape).

Verified: `cargo check --all-targets` clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). `cargo test --release`: 201 kovan lib tests passing (10 new calibration tests, all digitiser_synthetic integration tests still green, confirming the real end-to-end JSON pipeline is unaffected for AxisAligned data). `cargo doc --no-deps`: no new warnings. GUI binary rebuilt and smoke-tested under xvfb-run (same known no-GPU sandbox limitation as every other round this session). Regenerating the API doc mirror now. Not committed yet.

title: kovan: DECISION -- projective/parallelogram axis calibration for off-centre plots
